note: Three configurations were tried (gap 3's denyRead+allowWrite, denyRead+denyWrite with a broad allowWrite, and denyRead+denyWrite with no allowWrite). None gave a direct denial for a write into a denyRead-covered directory; each returned write_exit=0 with the host unchanged. Direct `Read-only file system` denial appeared only when denyWrite covered a path not also covered by denyRead (gap 1). Three configurations do not show that no configuration can give a direct denial, so the question in the next_check is narrowed, not settled. Remaining: other combinations (nested paths, per-file entries) or a source reading of how srt builds the bwrap mounts for denyRead.

results: Config (a) allowWrite=['.']+denyWrite=['overlap']+denyRead=['overlap']: write_exit=0 (from inside the sandbox); host-side overlap/ shows only the pre-existing marker.txt, newfile2.txt does not exist — same silent ephemeral-hide behavior as gap 3, even though denyWrite now also explicitly covers the path.

Config (b) allowWrite=[]+denyWrite=['overlap']+denyRead=['overlap'] (no allowWrite anywhere in the whole sandbox): write_exit=0 again; host-side newfile3.txt also does not exist — identical silent ephemeral-hide behavior even with no allowWrite grant at all.

No configuration tried (gap 3's original, plus these two) produced a direct denial (nonzero exit, 'Read-only file system'-style message) for a write into a denyRead-covered directory. Whenever filesystem.denyRead covers a directory, srt 0.0.77 appears to always mount an ephemeral overlay over it, silently absorbing writes (exit 0, host unchanged) regardless of denyWrite or allowWrite settings for that same path. Direct 'Read-only file system' denial (gap 1's receipt) only occurs when denyWrite applies WITHOUT denyRead covering the same path.
